Information Hierarchy: Live floor first; waiting parties at left; server roster and cover counts in context
Spatial Grammar: Dining areas contain positioned tables with capacity; drag or select a party to seat; assigned-server color and turn-time border stay on the table
State Vocabulary: Available; Seated; Ordered; Paid; Dirty; Blocked
Conflict Behavior: Overlapping reservations turn red; unavailable servers require an explicit swap before seating
Accessibility Alternative: Sortable table list with table, capacity, status, server, elapsed turn time, and compatible waiting parties
DPF Rationale: Adopt the live state and one-action seating grammar; adapt away from color-only status and long-press-only interaction

Information Hierarchy: Floor plan and waitlist are the shift command surface; shift overview and turn-time reporting remain secondary
Spatial Grammar: Custom floor plan with flexible table inventory, table types, server sections, and recommended assignments
State Vocabulary: Available inventory; assigned; seated; POS-derived table status; waiting; notified
Conflict Behavior: Recommendations expose compatible tables while inventory and pacing controls prevent overbooking
Accessibility Alternative: List of tables and parties with capacity, area, server section, status, quote, and recommendation reason
DPF Rationale: Adopt fast host-stand hierarchy and assignment recommendations; preserve operator confirmation and explain constraints

Information Hierarchy: Day calendar first; team members and resources form lanes; waitlist and gaps stay adjacent
Spatial Grammar: Time grid crosses staff and bookable resources such as chairs or rooms; appointments reserve service duration and buffers
State Vocabulary: Available; booked; blocked time; waiting; notified; in service; complete
Conflict Behavior: Staff skill, availability, resource, duration, and group alignment prevent overlap and double-booking
Accessibility Alternative: Agenda table grouped by provider with time, client, service, resource, status, gap, and conflict reason
DPF Rationale: Adopt provider-resource joint availability and intelligent gap filling; make chairs explicit resources and never rely on calendar position alone

Information Hierarchy: Staff appointments and resource availability stay together on the calendar; rooms, chairs, beds, and machines expose who is using them and when
Spatial Grammar: Staff and resource columns cross time; filters and drag-and-drop move an appointment to an available named resource while resource groups model interchangeable capacity
State Vocabulary: Available; scheduled; in use; unavailable; staff assigned; resource assigned
Conflict Behavior: Provider availability, service duration, required resource, group quantity, and resource availability constrain placement; allocation prevents double-booking and can select a compatible resource automatically
Accessibility Alternative: Agenda and resource table with staff, named resource or group, time, service, availability, assignment, and conflict reason, plus keyboard reassignment and confirmation
DPF Rationale: Adopt the joint provider-and-physical-resource schedule and allocation assistance; preserve an explicit assigned chair or resource and an accessible list instead of relying on column position

Information Hierarchy: Date occupancy summary first; room rows and reservation bars below; room condition, assigned housekeeper, maintenance needs, and unassigned accommodations remain visible in the shared calendar
Spatial Grammar: Rooms form rows across a date grid; reservation bars span stays; room and housekeeping state can be changed in place; search and filters preserve high-volume rack use
State Vocabulary: In-House; Confirmed; Checked Out; Dirty; Clean; Inspected; Out of Service; Maintenance Needed; Assigned Housekeeper; Unassigned Accommodation
Conflict Behavior: Reservation assignment remains distinct from housekeeping condition; unavailable inventory, maintenance needs, room type, stay overlap, and readiness constrain placement
Accessibility Alternative: Room operations table by date with room, reservation, arrival, departure, occupancy, housekeeping condition, housekeeper, maintenance need, and assignment state
DPF Rationale: Adopt the shared occupancy-and-housekeeping rack and explicit unassigned demand; preserve separate occupancy and condition fields, and pair every icon/color with text

Information Hierarchy: Reservation and arrival context lead; room assignment exposes matching inventory, room status, and housekeeping readiness before confirmation
Spatial Grammar: Room inventory is filtered by stay dates, room type, features, and operational status; attendants and housekeeping tasks remain linked to the physical room
State Vocabulary: Vacant clean; vacant dirty; occupied clean; occupied dirty; inspected; pickup; out of order; out of service; assigned; unassigned
Conflict Behavior: Stay overlap, room type or feature mismatch, out-of-order inventory, housekeeping readiness, and assignment locks block or warn before confirmation
Accessibility Alternative: Room assignment and housekeeping tables with room, type, stay dates, occupancy, housekeeping state, attendant, service task, restriction, and assignment action
DPF Rationale: Adopt joint reservation-room-housekeeping context and explicit readiness gates; keep guest-sensitive detail out of the shared spatial overview and require confirmation for reassignment

Information Hierarchy: Date, space type, and space number lead; reservation bars combine with occupancy, housekeeping, maintenance, and assignment state in one operational timeline
Spatial Grammar: Rooms form rows grouped by type and number across time; reservation bars, filters, drag-and-drop, and locked assignments support allocation while text labels accompany status color
State Vocabulary: Available; occupied; dirty; clean; inspected; out of order; out of service; assigned; unassigned; locked; overbooked
Conflict Behavior: Stay overlap, room type, out-of-order or out-of-service inventory, housekeeping readiness, and locked reservations constrain moves; optimization previews alternatives before applying them
Accessibility Alternative: Room timeline table by date and space with reservation span, occupancy, housekeeping state, maintenance restriction, assignment, lock, and conflict text, with keyboard assignment
DPF Rationale: Adopt the room rack and preview-before-apply allocation grammar; preserve explicit housekeeping and restriction labels, and exclude guest-sensitive detail from the shared overview

Information Hierarchy: Availability and location first; upcoming pickup/return fulfillment next; maintenance and performance remain visible
Spatial Grammar: Trackable units or bulk stock are grouped by product and location with a date-range availability horizon; barcode handoff changes custody
State Vocabulary: Available; reserved; picked; rented out; awaiting return; returned; downtime; maintenance
Conflict Behavior: Real-time availability prevents overbooking; buffers and downtime block unsafe adjacency; multi-location stock is separate
Accessibility Alternative: Inventory table with unit or quantity, product, location, availability range, custody state, next pickup/return, downtime, and conflict
DPF Rationale: Adopt unit identity, location, date-range availability, buffers, and downtime; add a spatial yard lens only where a business maintains meaningful bays

Information Hierarchy: Equipment availability, serialized identity, and current location lead; upcoming movements, shortages, subrentals, repairs, and loss remain visible before fulfillment
Spatial Grammar: A time horizon relates equipment or groups to projects and stock locations; QR, barcode, and serial scans record warehouse handoffs and movement across locations, people, and teams
State Vocabulary: Available; reserved; packed; collected; checked out; in transit; returned; repair; lost; subrented; shortage
Conflict Behavior: Quantity or serial availability across time and location, kit dependencies, repair or loss, and project demand expose shortages and drive alternative or subrental resolution
Accessibility Alternative: Searchable inventory table with product, quantity or serial, stock location, custody, state, next booking, shortage, repair, and movement history, with keyboard workflows
DPF Rationale: Adopt identity plus availability timeline plus location and movement as one operational model; expose shortage resolution and never depend on scan state or color alone

Information Hierarchy: Portfolio and association context first; maintenance and architectural requests flow into tracked work with board visibility
Spatial Grammar: Community and property locations anchor requests; work orders connect location, resident or common area, vendor, approvals, notes, and evidence
State Vocabulary: Submitted; triaged; assigned; scheduled; in progress; awaiting approval; complete; closed
Conflict Behavior: Priority, due date, board/vendor approval, access, budget, and duplicate-location work constrain action
Accessibility Alternative: Priority work table grouped by association/property with location, request, impact, due date, owner, vendor, approval, status, and next action
DPF Rationale: Adopt the property-linked system of record and mobile field evidence; elevate current priorities and blocked next actions above generic portfolio maps

Information Hierarchy: The selected association and property map lead; active violations, work orders, architectural requests, and past-cure items surface on each property before the manager opens details or starts an inspection
Spatial Grammar: An association-scoped map positions properties and permits multiple high-contrast status icons per property; search, recenter, current-location orientation, filters, and a list toggle support field navigation without making the map the action form
State Vocabulary: No active issue; active violation; active work order; active architectural request; past cure; selected property; offline; inspection in progress
Conflict Behavior: Association access and inspection permissions govern entry; multiple active issue types coexist instead of overwriting one another; filters reduce clutter while property details retain the full issue set and action path
Accessibility Alternative: Property priority list by address or proximity with text counts and labels for violations, work orders, architectural requests, past-cure state, next due action, and selection; icons never carry meaning by color alone
DPF Rationale: Adopt the association-bounded property map as a locator and priority-triage lens with an equivalent list; keep work decisions in the auditable detail workflow and exclude homeowner identity from the shared overview

Information Hierarchy: Unassigned Job Tray and alerts remain beside the technician schedule; teams, skills, zones, priorities, tags, and route context surface fit and exceptions before assignment
Spatial Grammar: Technicians form schedule lanes grouped by team while the route view supplies job order and travel context; jobs and non-job events move only into compatible technician windows
State Vocabulary: Unassigned; scheduled; dispatched; traveling; working; paused; complete; canceled; non-job event; alert; locked commitment
Conflict Behavior: Skill, business unit, team, zone, shift, availability, current job cycle, arrival window, traffic, capacity, overlaps, non-job events, and route efficiency constrain assignment
Accessibility Alternative: Dispatch table grouped by technician and team with job order, window, location, route estimate, skill and zone fit, state, priority, tag, conflict, and queued demand
DPF Rationale: Adopt queue-plus-schedule-plus-route grammar and visible job-cycle state; keep optimization advisory, explain skill/zone/time tradeoffs, and require confirmation for conflict-causing moves

Information Hierarchy: Schedule remains primary; the optimize action evaluates selected jobs and technicians, then previews route improvements before the dispatcher applies them
Spatial Grammar: Technician day routes combine appointment windows and job locations; drive-time optimization proposes a revised sequence while preserving the dispatcher as decision owner
State Vocabulary: Unassigned; scheduled; en route; in progress; completed; conflict; optimization proposed
Conflict Behavior: Appointment windows, technician assignment, start and end locations, locked jobs, overlaps, and increased drive time constrain the proposal; unresolved jobs stay queued
Accessibility Alternative: Technician schedule table with ordered jobs, appointment windows, locations, travel estimates, locked state, conflict reason, proposed order, and apply-or-reject action
DPF Rationale: Adopt preview-before-apply drive-time optimization and preserve queued demand; explain every moved job and never trade away promised windows silently
